leads.work: Logistics schedulers (Mary Poorman, Aimee Lannou, Jackie Young, Susan Hadix, Thu Nguyen) email the Texas desk (Daren Farmer) one by one to extend or create deals when gas flowed at a meter with no deal or nomination, so they can clear allocation exceptions or the 'UA4 list'
leads.why: A steady stream of nearly identical one-off requests (meter, days, last deal number, please extend), often about volumes of only a few Dth. Some go back to 1999. Each needs contract checks (Julie Meyers) and several rounds of replies. Flow on the first days after a shut-in, or valves not closed by 9am, keeps causing the same exception. This could be detected and given a default deal rule or strangers-gas rule automatically.

leads.work: Enerfin/TETCO meter 98-0439 volumes reallocated over and over between HPL, the East desk and Volume Management (retro deal extensions, OBA effective-date changes, Unify paths)
leads.why: Victor Lamadrid: 'We go round and round at this point changing volumes two, three or more times', and 'how often Enerfin's numbers change'. Long threads with many people over volumes of 9–141 Dth. HPL and TETCO allocation numbers don't match. The OBA date was changed retroactively without telling anyone.

leads.work: Approving write-offs of strangers gas to Unaccounted for Gas with a paper form (Clem Cernosek emails a form; the desk must print, sign and return the original)
leads.why: Many near-identical emails, one per meter, often for tiny or very old volumes (26 Mmbtu from 1999). Each needs a manual print-sign-return approval. This is a clear candidate for a batch or electronic approval workflow.

leads.work: Moving Canadian (ECC) deals booked in US books to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book; Stacey Vallejo sends deal IDs one at a time and invoicing waits until they're moved
leads.why: This keeps happening (Nov 1, Nov 27 and Dec 6–8 requests). Invoicing for ECC and ENA is held up each month. Darron forwards each request on to book admins by hand. A booking validation rule could stop it at the source.

leads.work: Arthur Andersen monthly gas testing: pulling P&L top sheets and curve shift reports for the top five days, book by book
leads.why: Requests come in month after month (August, September, October, Q3 close-out) and are passed down to book admins to pull together and photocopy. This could be a standard report that is generated automatically.

leads.work: Changing the EnerVest Sitara deal price (S#27239) every month when the invoice arrives
leads.why: Every month Tricia Truong asks for a new rate on the same deal (Sept, Oct, Nov 00, plus 1999 changes). Delays drew follow-up chasers. The price could be set by a formula or pulled in from the invoice.

leads.work: Emailing Schedule C reserve movements (amounts added or released) to Chris Abel, Daniel Falcone and Kenneth Thibodeaux
leads.why: Short notices that keep recurring ('We released $75M tonight', 'taking $100M to Schedule C'). Messages are forwarded by hand to extra people. This could be a system-generated notification.

leads.work: Nightly book officialization and V@R checks: each book admin checks positions, runs the 'official post id' macro, and controllers get an end-of-night sheet; lists of officialized books are kept by hand
leads.why: New manual control steps were added after V@R errors. Darron reminds the team it must be done 'every night'. He compiles book lists by hand for Connie Sutton, Susan Trevino and Russell Diamond. Credit also needs flat books officialized. There are complaints that INTRA-NORTHEAST-PHY was officialized four times.

leads.work: Daily Enovate DPR sign-off: confirming P&L and the net open position by email
leads.why: A recurring daily draft-and-confirm exchange ('Open position is 39.0 contracts').

leads.work: Cleaning up after system failures: Sitara bridge failures creating duplicate deals, TDS positions reloaded after downtime, manual monitoring of the bridge
leads.why: Book admins had to find and kill duplicate deals by hand, the same duplicates were still there the next day, and TDS position problems came up in the morning. Staff come in early to watch bridge releases.

leads.work: Setting up curves and books and changing portfolio hierarchies across ERMS, TAGG and RisktRAC with forms and emails
leads.why: Shona Wilson says the procedures are not being followed, with many curves found in ERMS that are missing from RisktRAC. Each new curve needs separate emails to have it added to TAGG. Book setup confirmations were re-forwarded to auditors. Naming conventions are handled by hand.

leads.work: System access and HR record maintenance requests (book run/print access, net send list, PEP supervisor and direct-report setup)
leads.why: Several back-and-forth emails to get access to the FT-Northwest book and to fix PEP reporting lines. Corporate analysts' records can't be changed by ENA HR, so a further handoff is needed.

leads.work: Settling counterparty pricing and billing disputes on old production months (HESCO underpayment, Samson invoices with no deal in Unify, TXU short-pays, Wyman Gordon billed with no deal, TGLO wash deals)
leads.why: Settlements staff chase the trading desk for prices or Sitara numbers months later, often because traders have left. One dispute was $32K. Threads run for weeks.

leads.work: Contract assignments and wrong-counterparty fixes (retro assignments moved by Volume Management, Cannon to Kinder Morgan, HPLC vs ENA entity errors)
leads.why: A process memo shows that retro assignments leave months of volumes to be moved by hand. Credit exposure stays wrong until the change is nominated. Schedulers can't change the counterparty themselves.

leads.work: Monthly third-party allocation and processing elections (CLECO/State Tract 121 meter netting, Big Thicket shrink, King Ranch elections, Indian Springs PVR backdated deals, checking King Ranch volumes)
leads.why: Monthly allocations done by hand that combine several meters. Someone asked who will do the monthly allocation. The same volumes are checked against each other's numbers.

leads.work: Month-end and recurring admin data calls (cost center allocation percentages, HR job survey and matching, PRC meetings, flash completion check, mapping traders to TAGG books, originator lists)
leads.why: Recurring data requests sent by mass email with short deadlines. The flash status is checked by polling each controller. The trader matrix was wanted 'by lunch'.

leads.work: Internal risk training classes (P&L/MiniBench, EOM bench, NGP&L) organized through repeated scheduling emails
leads.why: A recurring series that keeps slipping. Topics and dates are worked out by email each week. Process knowledge such as the steps for rolling the P&L lives only in people's heads, so it could be documented.

leads.work: Holiday and weather staffing: finding volunteers by reply-all, and reserving hotel rooms for bad weather
leads.why: Six reply-all messages just to staff one day. The weather-planning arrangements are made ad hoc.

leads.work: Recurring nominations and confirmations by email or Word doc (Calpine monthly nomination, Southern Union weekend sales recap, Aquila header confirmation, Cleco transport nominations)
leads.why: Nominations and confirmations exchanged as Word attachments or free-text email, which could be structured or electronic.

leads.work: Personal spreadsheets hard-wired to system names and directories (the SCADA server rename means everyone edits their NetDDE sheets; spreadsheet loads moving off the ng directory)
leads.why: Each user has to fix their own sheets by hand, and the new loading process had problems. This shows fragile end-user tools.

leads.work: Heavy forwarding of non-work chain email and jokes from work accounts (often re-forwarded to home addresses as well)
leads.why: A large share of this batch is jokes and chain mail that Darron and his colleagues forward, sometimes twice, often with large attachments (.exe, .mpg). This costs time and mailbox and network load.
